output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: ZipUtil$Unpacker.process, ZipUtil$BackslashUnpacker.process, ZipUtil$Unwraper.process, and Zips$UnpackingCallback.process all built the extraction destination as `new File(outputDir/destination, name)` directly from the (possibly NameMapper-rewritten) zip entry name, with no check that the resolved path stayed inside the intended output directory. A malicious archive entry with '../' segments (or other traversal sequences) could therefore write files anywhere the JVM process has write access.

Fix: added two small static helpers in ZipUtil.java —
  - `resolveEntryDestination(File outputDir, String name)`: builds `new File(outputDir, name)` and validates it.
  - `checkEntryDestination(File outputDir, File file, String name)`: validates an already-constructed File against outputDir (used by BackslashUnpacker's incremental per-segment path building, and reused by resolveEntryDestination).
Validation compares `file.getCanonicalPath()` against `outputDir.getCanonicalPath()` (equal, or a `File.separator`-prefixed descendant); canonicalization resolves '..' components and symlinks. On violation a `ZipException` (a RuntimeException, so no signature changes were needed) is thrown before any filesystem write happens (mkdir or copy).

All four sink locations from the alert (Unpacker, BackslashUnpacker's two branches, Unwraper) were updated to route through this check on the final resolved name. The sibling sink in Zips.java (Zips$UnpackingCallback, reachable via the public `Zips.destination(File).unpack()` API) has the identical unguarded pattern and CWE-022 root cause, so it was updated too by calling the now package-visible `ZipUtil.resolveEntryDestination`.

Added 4 regression tests to ZipUtilTest.java: relative '../' traversal blocked for `ZipUtil.unpack`, relative traversal blocked for `ZipUtil.unwrap`, backslash-traversal blocked for `ZipUtil.BackslashUnpacker`, and a test documenting that absolute-path entry names stay contained inside outputDir on this platform's `File(File,String)` resolution semantics (verified empirically; on Unix `new File(parent, absoluteChild)` concatenates rather than discarding the parent, so it isn't actually an escape vector here, but the test locks in that no file ever lands outside outputDir for that input too). Verified all existing tests still pass (120 total, only a pre-existing, unrelated FilePermissionsTest failure remains — confirmed present on the unpatched baseline too, caused by tests running as root in the container). Verified the supplied PoV (.security-pipeline/pov/ZipSlipPOV.java) now throws ZipException and exits 1 (blocked) instead of exiting 0 (exploited).
output_json.risk_notes: Behavioral change: extraction of a zip entry whose resolved destination path falls outside outputDir now throws ZipException instead of silently writing outside the target directory (previously undefined/unsafe behavior, never a supported use case). This could affect any caller that was unintentionally relying on such archives extracting successfully (e.g. malformed/malicious archives), which is the intended fix. Legitimate archives with only forward-relative entries are unaffected — full existing test suite (unpack, unwrap, BackslashUnpacker, Zips unpack, pack/repack round-trips) passes unchanged. The canonical-path check requires the output directory (or an ancestor) to exist/be resolvable via getCanonicalPath(); this matches prior behavior since outputDir is already expected to exist or be creatable in all call sites. No dependency or build-system changes.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-22 (Zip Slip / path traversal) in zt-zip's ZIP extraction sinks. Added a shared containment check (ZipUtil.resolveEntryDestination / checkEntryDestination) that resolves each extracted entry's destination File and verifies its canonical path is equal to, or a descendant of, the canonical path of the target output directory, throwing ZipException otherwise. Applied this check at all root-cause sinks identified in the alert: ZipUtil$Unpacker.process (used by all unpack(File/InputStream, File[, Charset|NameMapper]) overloads), ZipUtil$BackslashUnpacker.process (both the backslash-split per-segment loop and the plain-name else branch), and ZipUtil$Unwraper.process (used by unwrap(...) overloads). Also fixed the same unguarded 'new File(destination, entryName)' pattern in the sibling extraction sink Zips$UnpackingCallback.process (used by the public Zips.destination(File).unpack() API), which shares the identical CWE-22 root cause though it wasn't explicitly in the alert traces. The check runs on the final (NameMapper-mapped) name, uses canonical-path comparison (resolves symlinks, unlike lexical/string-prefix checks), and covers both the mkdir (directory entry) and file-copy code paths.
